source: ggml-org/llama.cpp CMake options; intended to be refreshed against upstream

switches.name: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE
switches.description: Selects the overall CMake build mode. Release is the normal choice for a production llama.cpp build; Debug is useful when diagnosing code or backend faults.
switches.meaningful_description: Selects the overall CMake build mode. Release is the normal choice for a production llama.cpp build; Debug is useful when diagnosing code or backend faults.
switches.recommendation: Release is the normal recommended choice.
switches.caution: Use Release for production. Debug builds are slower and larger.

switches.name: GGML_NATIVE
switches.description: Allows the CPU backend to use instruction sets available on this exact build machine. It can improve host-side performance but makes the resulting binaries less portable to other CPUs.
switches.meaningful_description: Allows the CPU backend to use instruction sets available on this exact build machine. It can improve host-side performance but makes the resulting binaries less portable to other CPUs.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for a machine-specific build; avoid for portable binaries.
switches.caution: Do not use when the build will be copied to older or different CPUs.

switches.name: GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS
switches.description: Builds multiple CPU variants so a binary can select an appropriate implementation at run time instead of being tied to one CPU target.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds multiple CPU variants so a binary can select an appropriate implementation at run time instead of being tied to one CPU target.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for portable CPU packages, not normally needed for an accelerator-first local build.
switches.caution: Increases build size and compile time.

switches.name: GGML_OPENMP
switches.description: Enables OpenMP support for parallel CPU work. Accelerator builds still contain CPU-side work, so this can matter for preprocessing and fallback operations.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables OpenMP support for parallel CPU work. Accelerator builds still contain CPU-side work, so this can matter for preprocessing and fallback operations.
switches.recommendation: Normally keep enabled unless a toolchain or deployment forbids OpenMP.
switches.caution: Adds OpenMP runtime requirements.

switches.name: GGML_CUDA
switches.description: Builds the NVIDIA CUDA backend so supported NVIDIA GPUs can execute llama.cpp workloads through CUDA.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the NVIDIA CUDA backend so supported NVIDIA GPUs can execute llama.cpp workloads through CUDA.
switches.recommendation: Required for native CUDA acceleration.
switches.caution: Requires a compatible NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit.

switches.name: GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS
switches.description: Enables CUDA graph execution where llama.cpp can capture repeated GPU work into graphs, reducing launch overhead for suitable workloads.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables CUDA graph execution where llama.cpp can capture repeated GPU work into graphs, reducing launch overhead for suitable workloads.
switches.recommendation: Good default on supported CUDA systems; disable when debugging graph-related issues.
switches.caution: Not every workload benefits equally.

switches.name: GGML_CUDA_FA
switches.description: Compiles CUDA FlashAttention support to accelerate attention operations on supported NVIDIA hardware.
switches.meaningful_description: Compiles CUDA FlashAttention support to accelerate attention operations on supported NVIDIA hardware.
switches.recommendation: Recommended when the CUDA toolchain and GPU support it.
switches.caution: Adds CUDA compilation work.

switches.name: GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS
switches.description: Adds additional quantised FlashAttention kernel variants beyond the normal set. This trades build time and binary size for broader quantisation coverage.
switches.meaningful_description: Adds additional quantised FlashAttention kernel variants beyond the normal set. This trades build time and binary size for broader quantisation coverage.
switches.recommendation: Leave off unless the intended models need the extra kernels.
switches.caution: Can substantially increase compilation time.

switches.name: GGML_CUDA_NCCL
switches.description: Adds NVIDIA NCCL collective communication support for configurations that need fast communication across multiple CUDA devices or distributed workers.
switches.meaningful_description: Adds NVIDIA NCCL collective communication support for configurations that need fast communication across multiple CUDA devices or distributed workers.
switches.recommendation: Use only when multiple GPUs or distributed execution needs NCCL.
switches.caution: Unnecessary for a single-GPU build.

switches.name: GGML_HIP
switches.description: Builds the AMD HIP/ROCm backend for supported discrete AMD GPUs.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the AMD HIP/ROCm backend for supported discrete AMD GPUs.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for supported discrete AMD GPUs.
switches.caution: Do not assume an integrated Radeon is ROCm-capable.

switches.name: GGML_HIP_GRAPHS
switches.description: Enables HIP graph execution to reduce repeated dispatch overhead on supported ROCm workloads.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables HIP graph execution to reduce repeated dispatch overhead on supported ROCm workloads.
switches.recommendation: Good candidate after a basic HIP build is verified.
switches.caution: Keep off when diagnosing HIP graph issues.

switches.name: GGML_HIP_RCCL
switches.description: Adds ROCm RCCL support for collective communication between multiple AMD GPUs or distributed workers.
switches.meaningful_description: Adds ROCm RCCL support for collective communication between multiple AMD GPUs or distributed workers.
switches.recommendation: Enable only when multi-GPU communication needs it.
switches.caution: Not useful on a single GPU.

switches.name: GGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN
switches.description: Enables rocWMMA-based FlashAttention kernels on supported AMD architectures.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables rocWMMA-based FlashAttention kernels on supported AMD architectures.
switches.recommendation: Treat as an architecture-specific optimisation and benchmark it.
switches.caution: May not apply to every AMD GPU.

switches.name: GGML_VULKAN
switches.description: Builds the cross-vendor Vulkan backend. It is useful when a vendor-native backend is unavailable, unsupported, or when one build should cover several GPU vendors.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the cross-vendor Vulkan backend. It is useful when a vendor-native backend is unavailable, unsupported, or when one build should cover several GPU vendors.
switches.recommendation: Useful as a portability or alternative backend.
switches.caution: Requires working Vulkan development/runtime support.

switches.name: GGML_VULKAN_VALIDATE
switches.description: Enables Vulkan validation layers so incorrect API usage and resource problems can be diagnosed during development.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables Vulkan validation layers so incorrect API usage and resource problems can be diagnosed during development.
switches.recommendation: Enable for diagnosis, not normal production builds.
switches.caution: Requires Vulkan validation layers.

switches.name: GGML_VULKAN_DEBUG
switches.description: Enables additional Vulkan backend debug output intended to help diagnose device and command issues.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables additional Vulkan backend debug output intended to help diagnose device and command issues.
switches.recommendation: Enable temporarily when investigating a Vulkan fault.
switches.caution: Produces extra output.

switches.name: GGML_VULKAN_CHECK_RESULTS
switches.description: Adds extra checks around Vulkan operation results so backend problems can be detected earlier.
switches.meaningful_description: Adds extra checks around Vulkan operation results so backend problems can be detected earlier.
switches.recommendation: Useful when validating a new Vulkan device or driver.
switches.caution: Adds checking overhead.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL
switches.description: Builds the SYCL accelerator backend used by Intel GPU configurations through oneAPI and Level Zero.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the SYCL accelerator backend used by Intel GPU configurations through oneAPI and Level Zero.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for the detected Arc A770 on this machine.
switches.caution: Requires a working oneAPI SYCL compiler and Level Zero stack.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL_TARGET
switches.description: Selects the SYCL target family expected by the backend. For Intel oneAPI builds this is normally INTEL.
switches.meaningful_description: Selects the SYCL target family expected by the backend. For Intel oneAPI builds this is normally INTEL.
switches.recommendation: Use INTEL for Intel oneAPI/Arc builds.
switches.caution: Do not change casually; it is backend-specific.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL_DEVICE_ARCH
switches.description: Allows explicit device architecture selection when the SYCL compiler needs a particular target rather than its default device set.
switches.meaningful_description: Allows explicit device architecture selection when the SYCL compiler needs a particular target rather than its default device set.
switches.recommendation: Usually leave automatic unless a known device target is required.
switches.caution: An incorrect architecture can make the build unusable.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL_F16
switches.description: Enables 16-bit floating-point paths in the SYCL backend where supported, potentially reducing memory traffic and improving throughput.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables 16-bit floating-point paths in the SYCL backend where supported, potentially reducing memory traffic and improving throughput.
switches.recommendation: Consider after the base SYCL build is stable and benchmark results justify it.
switches.caution: Results depend on model and GPU support.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL_GRAPH
switches.description: Enables graph execution support in the SYCL backend for repeated accelerator work.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables graph execution support in the SYCL backend for repeated accelerator work.
switches.recommendation: Good candidate for performance testing after a stable build.
switches.caution: Disable when troubleshooting graph behaviour.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL_SUPPORT_LEVEL_ZERO
switches.description: Enables Intel Level Zero support through the SYCL backend, providing the native low-level path needed for Intel GPU device interaction.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables Intel Level Zero support through the SYCL backend, providing the native low-level path needed for Intel GPU device interaction.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for Intel GPU builds.
switches.caution: Requires the Level Zero loader and headers.

switches.name: GGML_SYCL_DNN
switches.description: Enables oneDNN integration in the SYCL backend for supported accelerated operations.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables oneDNN integration in the SYCL backend for supported accelerated operations.
switches.recommendation: Recommended when oneDNN is present and stable.
switches.caution: Adds oneDNN dependency and linking complexity.

switches.name: GGML_OPENCL
switches.description: Builds the OpenCL backend for accelerators that expose compatible OpenCL devices.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the OpenCL backend for accelerators that expose compatible OpenCL devices.
switches.recommendation: Useful as an alternative backend when OpenCL is the best supported path.
switches.caution: Usually prefer a native vendor backend when available.

switches.name: GGML_OPENCL_PROFILING
switches.description: Enables OpenCL profiling support so kernel execution timing can be inspected during tuning.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables OpenCL profiling support so kernel execution timing can be inspected during tuning.
switches.recommendation: Use for benchmarking and diagnostics, not always for production.
switches.caution: Adds profiling overhead.

switches.name: GGML_OPENCL_EMBED_KERNELS
switches.description: Embeds OpenCL kernels into the build so the resulting program carries its kernel source/assets rather than relying on separate files.
switches.meaningful_description: Embeds OpenCL kernels into the build so the resulting program carries its kernel source/assets rather than relying on separate files.
switches.recommendation: Useful when packaging a portable OpenCL application.
switches.caution: Increases binary size.

switches.name: GGML_OPENCL_USE_ADRENO_KERNELS
switches.description: Enables specialised Adreno OpenCL kernels intended for Qualcomm Adreno devices.
switches.meaningful_description: Enables specialised Adreno OpenCL kernels intended for Qualcomm Adreno devices.
switches.recommendation: Use only when an Adreno accelerator is detected.
switches.caution: Not relevant to Intel or AMD PC GPUs.

switches.name: GGML_OPENVINO
switches.description: Builds the OpenVINO backend, allowing supported Intel devices and workloads to use the OpenVINO runtime.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the OpenVINO backend, allowing supported Intel devices and workloads to use the OpenVINO runtime.
switches.recommendation: Useful when OpenVINO is the chosen runtime path rather than SYCL.
switches.caution: Requires a compatible OpenVINO installation.

switches.name: GGML_RPC
switches.description: Builds remote procedure call backend support so work can be delegated to a remote backend service.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds remote procedure call backend support so work can be delegated to a remote backend service.
switches.recommendation: Use only when remote execution is part of the design.
switches.caution: Adds networking and deployment complexity.

switches.name: GGML_BACKEND_DL
switches.description: Builds backends as dynamically loadable components so one installation can load backend libraries at run time.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds backends as dynamically loadable components so one installation can load backend libraries at run time.
switches.recommendation: Useful for a flexible multi-backend deployment.
switches.caution: Adds runtime library management complexity.

switches.name: BUILD_SHARED_LIBS
switches.description: Requests shared libraries for CMake targets that honour this setting, which is useful for applications that dynamically link against llama.cpp libraries.
switches.meaningful_description: Requests shared libraries for CMake targets that honour this setting, which is useful for applications that dynamically link against llama.cpp libraries.
switches.recommendation: Useful when another application will link to llama.cpp dynamically.
switches.caution: May complicate standalone distribution.

switches.name: GGML_BUILD_TESTS
switches.description: Builds the project test targets used to validate ggml and backend behaviour.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds the project test targets used to validate ggml and backend behaviour.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for development; optional for a minimal production build.
switches.caution: Adds build time and can expose unrelated test-link dependencies.

switches.name: GGML_BUILD_EXAMPLES
switches.description: Builds examples and related tools shipped with llama.cpp, including useful command-line utilities.
switches.meaningful_description: Builds examples and related tools shipped with llama.cpp, including useful command-line utilities.
switches.recommendation: Recommended for a development build; optional for a minimal runtime-only package.
switches.caution: Adds build time and extra targets.
